subject: Pricing follow-up: token volumes & $/1M benchmarking (Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic)
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-20T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing follow-up: token volumes & $/1M benchmarking (Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic)

Hi Samir — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps on pricing so we can align on a pilot: 

1) Your expected volumes (from the call): ~300M generation tokens/month (peak 12M/day), 50M embedding tokens/month.
2) Primary goal: deterministic unit economics for the product team — target overall infra budget of roughly $8k-$16k/month for inference during the pilot.
3) You asked for raw $/1M-token benchmarks (generation tokens) vs common providers and what reserved/pilot pricing could look like.

Attached is a concise pricing model (redwood_pricing_model_v2.xlsx) with three options:
- Pay-as-you-go (hosted) — baseline RB pricing (no commit).
- 3-mo pilot commitment — discounted unit rate.
- Reserved baseline (6–12 mo) — best unit economics with capacity guarantee.

Benchmark summary (high level):
- OpenAI (hosted, similar model family) — list price we used for comparison: ~$18 / 1M generation tokens.*
- Anthropic (hosted) — list price used: ~$20 / 1M generation tokens.*
- Open-model hosts (self-hosted / managed) — broad band depending on quantization, caching and infra: ~$6–$12 / 1M.
- Redwood target for pilot (3 mo commit): $7–$9 / 1M generation tokens (includes KV caching and prefix optimization assumptions).

Notes/assumptions: 
- Benchmarks here are simplified per-token comparisons — actual unit economics depend heavily on prompt length distribution, caching hit-rate, batching, and whether you use generation+embedding mixed workloads.
- The attached workbook includes a runbook where you can plug your expected prompt-length distribution to get per-featureized estimated costs.

Requested next items from your side: 
- Confirm expected 1) baseline monthly generation tokens and 2) whether embeddings are billed separately (you mentioned embeddings will be for DBA indexing and are lower priority).
- Confirm whether a 3-month pilot with a committed floor is feasible vs pay-as-you-go.

If you’re good, we (Marissa + Aditya) can draft a short mutual action plan and a pilot SOW that mirrors the $/1M targets and the acceptance criteria you described.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20m call if you want to walk the workbook together.
— Vanessa Ortiz
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0192

Attachment: redwood_pricing_model_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet, 3 sheets — summary, assumptions, runbook)

From: Samir Patel <samir@acme.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-20T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: token volumes & $/1M benchmarking (Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic)

Hi Vanessa — thanks for the clear recap and the workbook. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Volumes: our conservative estimate for the first 3 months is ~250–350M generation tokens/month (varies by day; weekend traffic lower). Embeddings: ~40–60M tokens/month — we expect embeddings costs to be relatively steady and separate.
2) Budget: for a short pilot we were budgeting $8k–$12k/month for inference licensing (not including internal infra egress/storage). If we see strong latency/quality gains we could expand the budget.
3) Benchmarks: the OpenAI/Anthropic numbers you listed align with what we’ve seen; our internal infra team thinks self-hosted costs (if we manage infra) could land around $7–$10/1M with heavy quantization and maximizing caching, but that requires engineering bandwidth.

We're inclined to try a 3-month pilot if Redwood can hit ~$8/1M for generation tokens (pilot commitment with a modest floor and simple SLA). That would make the month-over-month spend for 300M tokens ~ $2,400 — which is attractive against our internal TCO when factoring dev ops costs.

Next: Please send a pilot MOU + an example mutual action plan; we’ll route for legal/procurement if numbers look ok. Also please flag any hard limits in the pilot (max throughput, latency SLO).

Thanks,
Samir
Head of Product, Acme AI
samir@acme.ai

Attachment: acme_estimates_summary.pdf (1 page — conservative volumes & budget range)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@acme.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-21T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: token volumes & $/1M benchmarking (Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic)

Morning Samir — looping in a quick commercial option set we can execute fast. Vanessa and I discussed and recommend the following pilot structure to meet your target ~$8/1M: 

Pilot Option A — 3-mo commitment (recommended)
- Committed floor: 50M generation tokens/mo (billed monthly)
- Variable usage above floor charged at $8 / 1M generation tokens
- Embeddings billed at $10 / 1M tokens (separate metric)
- Includes basic latency SLO (p95 < 450ms) and priority onboarding support

Pilot Option B — PAYG short pilot
- No commit floor; $11 / 1M generation tokens (hosted)
- Embeddings $12 / 1M
- Best for teams that want zero contractual commitment but pay higher unit rates

Enterprise Reserved (for reference)
- 6–12 mo commits with unit rates down to $5–$6 / 1M depending on capacity commit and burst lanes

Operational notes: 
- The $8 / 1M assumes caching and moderate batching benefits; we’ll run a 3-day validation load test against your expected prompt distribution (runbook in the workbook).
- If you hit sustained higher QPS (e.g., >15k token/sec sustained) we’ll recommend moving to a dedicated pool with predictable latency and an adjusted pricing band.

If Option A looks good I’ll draft a short MOU and mutual action plan we can sign electronically (DocuSign). I’ve attached an updated pricing workbook with the Option A math tab.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood_pricing_model_v2.xlsx (updated; Option A tab)

From: Samir Patel <samir@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-21T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: token volumes & $/1M benchmarking (Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic)

Thanks Marissa / Vanessa — Option A looks reasonable. We can start with a 3-mo pilot with the floor you propose. Please go ahead and share the MOU and the mutual action plan; procurement will want the unit rates and the acceptance criteria included (load test pass, latency SLO, and validation dataset).

One more ask: do you have a short one-page comparison that calls out total cost examples for 100M / 300M / 600M tokens per month versus OpenAI and Anthropic (so our CFO sees the delta)? That would help speed approval.

Samir
